title: Law of Sines Practice
description: Practice using the Law of Sines for ASA, AAS, and selected SSA cases.

questions.question: Which formula is the Law of Sines for △ABC?
options: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C
questions.explanation: The Law of Sines compares each side with the sine of its opposite angle.

questions.question: Which given case usually points directly to the Law of Sines after finding the third angle?
questions.explanation: ASA gives two angles and a side. After finding the third angle, you can match known and unknown opposite pairs.

questions.question: In △ABC, ∠A = 44° and ∠B = 71°. What is ∠C?
questions.explanation: The angles of a triangle sum to 180°, so C = 180° - 44° - 71° = 65°.

questions.question: In △ABC, ∠A = 50°, ∠B = 60°, and a = 14. Which equation correctly solves for b?
questions.explanation: Pair a with A and b with B: b/sin 60° = 14/sin 50°, so b = 14 sin 60° / sin 50°.

questions.question: In △ABC, ∠A = 50°, ∠B = 60°, and a = 14. What is b to the nearest tenth?
In △ABC, ∠A = 32°, ∠C = 88°, and c = 20. What is a to the nearest tenth?
In the SSA case, inverse sine may give one angle even when a second triangle is also possible.
questions.explanation: Two supplementary angles can have the same sine value, so SSA requires a second-angle check.

questions.question: In △ABC, ∠A = 38°, ∠B = 72°, and a = 9. Find b to the nearest tenth.
In △ABC, ∠A = 42°, a = 11, and b = 8. Find ∠B to the nearest tenth of a degree.
questions.explanation: sin B = 8 sin 42° / 11 ≈ 0.4866, so B ≈ 29.1°. The supplementary angle is impossible because it would make the angle sum exceed 180°.

questions.question: Explain why a computed value like sin B = 1.08 means no triangle is possible.
questions.correctAnswer: No triangle is possible because the sine of an angle cannot be greater than 1.
questions.explanation: For real triangle angles, sine values must stay between -1 and 1. A value above 1 signals impossible measurements.
